Emmy Ryder palaa kotitilalleen Wyomingin Meadowlarkiin kaiken menettäneenä. Unelmien ura hevosten parissa on tyssännyt loukkaantumiseen. Kun Emmy kohtaa paikallisessa pubissa veljensä parhaan ystävän Luken, lapsuusvuosiensa kiusankappaleen, hän tuntee yllättäen tähän välittömästi vetoa. Mutta Luke on ylimielinen paha poika, ja kaiken lisäksi he ovat lähestulkoon perheenjäseniä!

Myös Luke panee merkille ystävänsä pikkusiskon eikä saa silmiään irti hänestä, mutta yrittää tukahduttaa himonsa. Mutta entä jos Luke on juuri sitä, mitä Emmy tarvitsee päästäkseen takaisin satulaan?

Booktokin valloittaneen kuuman cowboy-romantiikkasarjan avauksessa veljen paras kaveri herättää yllättäviä tunteita.

I don't think I'm asking for too much when it comes to romance. I want banter, I want sizzle, and I want swoon. And yet, somehow, I keep coming across romance books with none of the above.

Emmy was thrown from her horse during barrel racing, so she's now back at her family's ranch recovering mentally from the accident and figuring out her next steps. Of course there's a cute boy next door who just happens to be her brothers' best friend and totally off-limits. All of a sudden, sparks are flying and Emmy and Luke can't help falling for each other.

Okay that's a great premise. But right off the bat, there's a problem. Where are the sparks? I detected not an ounce of sizzle or tension anywhere in here. The characters were bland, their conversations were bland, and I had a hard time imagining anyone falling in love or lust while saying such bland and boring things to each other.

A large part of the problem is the writing style. It essentially intercuts scenes inside the characters' heads (where they constantly go on and on about how beautiful the other person is and how attracted they are to them), with the aforementioned bland dialogue, with some additional scenes of them talking to their BFFs about how much they like the other person. It was just tell, tell, tell, with no show at all.

The things is, tension (romantic or otherwise) always comes from what is unsaid, not what is said. So if you have a story that is all tell and no show and essentially overshares and overexplains the feelings that the characters have for each other, then you have effectively killed good and dead the most important element in a story.

Another issue is the characters. It's not that they're unlikable, because that would mean there is something to dislike. It's more that they feel generic, like cardboard cutouts of what romance leads should be. Luke is nice and handsome and always there to lend a hand, while Emmy has deep-seated issues that Luke will inevitably swoop in and make all better. I guess I just expected a little bit more.

Even the cowboy element felt so bland. If you take out the fact that they're on a ranch and Luke wore a cowboy hat once in the whole story, and substitute a different sport for barrel racing, this would literally be any other romance. I don't think there was even a single cowboy expression or "yeehaw!" in here.

The other thing that was disappointing was the ADHD rep. There was specifically an author's note at the beginning of the book talking about how she has ADHD, and she wrote Emmy with that in mind. I'm always so heartened to see diverse representation in books, so when Emmy's ADHD turned out to be little more than her being messy and late to things, it felt lacking.

I'm sorry, but this book did not live up to the hype. Sure, if you're wanting a generic romance with some horses thrown in, there's nothing wrong with this one. But if you're hoping for even a little bit more, you're better off looking somewhere else.

A bit boring, unoriginal, with lots of overused phrases that can probably be found in hundreds of romance novels these days. These are the first things that came to my mind after finishing it, because seriously, you could find hundreds of almost identical books, but I still somehow enjoyed it to some extent as I basically read it in two days.


I think the book could have been more enjoyable if the main characters were more likeable. The heroine was okay, even though some of her actions were just stupid, but the hero? This guy was insufferable most of the time.

"Emmy is in Meadowlark?” Gus’s tone was tight. Shit. I definitely threw Emmy under the bus.
“Yeah, she left my bar with Kenny Wyatt last night.” Again, shit."


You definitely threw her under the bus.

"I felt the smallest of smiles tug at the corners of my mouth, thinking about Luke Brooks having to ask that girl to drive him to go pick up his best friend’s little sister."


He shows up tipsy and late with his hookup to take you home because his best friend asked him to, and you smile at the memory because at least he showed up? The bar is in hell.


The writing style was entertaining enough to keep me engaged in the story, although I still skipped some things because I didn't care about them, but some of the sentences here were painful to read.

"You can take it, sugar. I’ll go slow.”


Is this sentence a requirement in romance books nowadays? I've seen this exact phrase in at least hundreds of romances.

"How much do I owe you?” she asked.
“On the house.”
“You sure?” she asked."


It’s literally the TikTok sound. The originality is dead in books these days.


Honestly, I picked up this book because the second story is coming out in a few days and I wanted to see if this series is worth reading, and now I'm not even sure if I'll read it. Maybe, maybe not. I remember liking some of the books in the Chestnut Springs series from Elsie Silver and I feel like Lyla Sage took a lot of inspiration from it, so like I said, maybe I'll read the second book, because it might be the same situation as in the Chestnut series, in which some books worked for me and others didn't. We’ll see.

3 Stars ★

“ You deserve to go out on your own terms. Just because you got dusted doesn’t mean you’re done.”


This gave me major Yellowstone vibes, and I'm not mad about it. From the description of the ranch, the background and other reasons that I won't give away. I ate this up for those very reasons.

Done and Dusted is the first book in the Rebel Blue Ranch series. This roped me in with the small town, brother's best friend, cowboy romance that was fast-paced, cute, and fluffy with just the right amount of tension and banter. I simply had a hard time putting it down.

Emmy returned home to her family's ranch, Rebel Blue, in Meadowlark Wyoming after an accident she had. She hadn't told anyone what had happened since she'd been home. One day, while in the stable on the ranch, her brother's best friend Luke witnesses her being uncomfortable with her horse. He finds out that she is unable to ride since the accident happened and offers to help her trust her skills again by giving her lessons to teach her to ride again. Will their lessons turn into more?


Clementine "Emmy" Ryder is a champion barrel racer who is suffering from trauma after the accident she had. She is kind and caring, often times putting on a facquade that nothing is wrong with the ones she holds dear. While inside, she is struggling with her adhd, getting lost in her thoughts and the quiet. I didn't connect with her on a personal level, but I did enjoy her and her witty comebacks that made me giggle.

“I thought it would get better. I really thought it would get better.”


Luke Brooks is a cowboy on Rebel Blue Ranch and the owner of the local bar Devils Boot. He has a lot on his plate but doesn't let it show always showing up and helping out when needed. Luke acted like he didn't care, but deep down, he has the biggest heart and is protective over the ones he holds dear. The only thing that I didn't care much about him was the nickname sugar it was overused, and it just made me feel sick. I will never like that nickname from another book taking it to another level, iykyk.

"I didn’t really know how to be in love, but I knew I wanted to be with Emmy in every way I could."


Emmy and Luke didn't like each other at first, built a friendship, then quickly became lovers, making it feel very insta-love. If we had gotten to see more of them and their moments, it wouldn't have felt this way so much. Though they moved fast, the spice was a delicious slowburn that I was here for. I did love that though they grew up together, he never once viewed or referred to her as his sister. It was always his best friend's sister. I did enjoy their banter, tension, and the way that they helped one another.

“I’m serious, Emmy. I don’t know when it happened, but I like you. I like you a lot more than I fucking should, and I know we shouldn’t do this because a million things could go wrong, but you feel so right.”


The ending was cute but didn't seem unique to me. I did enjoy this and was happy that there wasn't a third act conflict. This was exactly what I was looking for, though some of it didn't appear to be original. This being her debut I'm hoping the next to come have more originality.


Favorite Quotes and moments

“You didn’t ask me why I came home.”
“I don’t care why you’re here, only that you are.”

“When it came to Emmy, I was playing with fire, but I would happily walk into the flames for her. And I’d have a smile on my face the whole damn time."

“You know, if you don’t like the road you’re on, you can always pave a new one.”

"I couldn’t believe the universe was so big, and I got placed on this random floating rock at the same time as Clementine Ryder."

“I’ve been people’s dirty little secret before, and I didn’t care because I didn’t care about them, but I care about you.”

“Thank you,” he continued, “for taking care of my baby girl.”
“She can take care of herself,” I said. “I know she can, but you made sure she didn’t have to do it alone.”

“I couldn’t believe the universe was so big, and I got placed on this random floating rock at the same time as Clementine Ryder.”

This book is super cute, and had adorable, wholesome small town moments and Ryder family moments, all the fluff and steamy scenes, and the heartwarming romance story that I needed. Also this had brother's bestfriend trope with a pinch of hate to love relationship.


“I know we shouldn’t do this because a million things could go wrong, but you feel so right.”



I enjoyed the story though I was a little bore in between the chapters. The characters were written so well considering that it is Lyla's debut novel The pacing was fast which why I liked it even more. I wish we got scenes where they were working together to get more natural sense of their relationship and slow burn romance.


➸ Luke Brooks

Broody bar owner and a Cowboy in Meadowlark 🤠 this man is just perfect and damn the things he did for Emmy and everyone made him even more than just perfect. T-shirt mutilator and careless Luke is everything you need because no matter how he tries to show he doesn't care but he does and so deeply that he would do anything to help his loved ones. His thoughtful and protective side was just so adorable 🥺💘 I really need find myself a Luke Brooks because who doesn't love a hot and thoughtful cowboy in their bed with a dirty dirty mouth.


“When it came to Emmy, I was playing with fire, but I would happily walk into the flames for her. And I’d have a smile on my face the whole damn time.”



➸ Emmy Ryder

A horse rider who is back in her hometown after her accident while riding. I didn’t felt much connected to her in the start but she did grew on me slowly throughout the book. She is grumpy, sassy and loves to be in control but when Luke entered her life everything changed for the better for her and I liked how she never denied what she felt for him but actually acted on those feelings.


“Luke wasn’t my secret. He was just mine.”



╰┈➤ Luke and Emmy

Luke and Emmy were amazing. Their hate to love dynamics and banter added more tension and spice to their romance. He never thought of her as his little sister even when she was young, it was always Gus's little sister and his “SUGAR” for him. They helped each other and start trusting each other more and knowing more about each other and bringing out each other's soft sides. But I wish we actually get to read those scenes. They were kind of skipped over.


“Fuck off, Brooks.” He let out a low whistle that ended in a chuckle. I hated when he did that. “Glad to see your tongue is still sharp as ever, sugar.” The way he said “sugar” was almost demeaning.
“Don’t. Call. Me. That.” I paused after every word, letting my annoyance with Brooks punctuate every syllable.



Their relationship developed from kind of enemies to friends to lovers. Luke always cared about her since they were little kids and he did in his own way which always pissed Emmy. They were always there for each other no matter what 🥺💘 Emmy Luke's love was steady and slow and perfect the way they are for each other.

4 ⭐️ A sweet and very sexy debut western romance


"Even if you weren't in my bar, you would be my business. You've always been my business, and you'll always be my business."


WHAT TO EXPECT:
✨ cowboy romance
✨ Wyoming ranch setting
✨ he's a reformed bad boy and owner of the local bar
✨ she's a barrel racer returning home after a scary fall
✨ brother's best friend
✨ forbidden love
✨ he falls first
✨ annoyance to love
✨ "I can't stay away from you anymore"
✨ amazing banter
✨ 3/5 spice
✨ found family
✨ ADHD rep and sensory issues (fmc)
✨ dual pov
✨ low angst
✨ HEA


My Thoughts:

I’m usually not a huge country, small-town romance girlie, but I am now!!! I absolutely adore this story! The characters are so lovable, the spice is top-tier (don't let the innocent cover fool you), and the writing makes you feel like you're transported to Rebel Blue Ranch in Meadowlark, Wyoming. It's low angst and high swoon - the perfect feel-good book!⁠
⁠
Luke and Emmy totally have my heart. These two have so much chemistry and I LOVED their banter.

I found Emmy to be so relatable, and I really appreciate how this story addresses ADHD, anxiety, and trauma. 👏⁠
⁠
And Luke is . . . good lord, this man is just so f**king HOT. The words that come out of his mouth are absolutely filthy. For example:

“Stop staring at my cock like that, sugar.”
My eyes shot back up to Brooks. “L-like what?”
“Like you want me to put you on your knees and shove it down your throat.”🥵


I also never knew being called sugar was fucking sexy until I read this book.

“Tell me you’re mine, Emmy.” I needed to hear it.
“I’m yours.”
“That’s right, sugar. I’m the only one that gets to have you like this.” 💕


I've also never read a story where I fall in love with every single side character. Wes, Teddy, Amos, Gus, Riley, and Hank are all so wonderful in their own ways, and I liked how Lyla explored the different relationships the MCs have with each of these characters. And while I love them all, Wes is definitely my favorite with his loyal, quiet, but sexy, golden retriever energy!!!!!!! I seriously need his book, Swift and Saddled, ASAP!


This is one hell of a debut novel, and I'm so proud of Lyla Sage for creating this beautiful world!!! You crushed it, babe!!

Thank you so much Lyla Sage for an ARC in exchange for an honest review. As always, all opinions are my own.

I didn't really know how to be in love, but I knew that I wanted to be with Emmy, in every way that I could. I wanted the kitchen slow dances, night out with shots, rides through the mountains, hot sex, afternoon naps, two-lane highways with the windows down. I wanted it all.
_______

Luke wasn't my secret. He was just mine.
_______

"That's right, sugar. Keep riding me."
_______
